sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: An iconic tree endemic to Socotra in the Indian Ocean. It reaches about 10 m and develops a dense, umbrella-shaped crown 4–8 m across.

sections.title: Foliage and flowering
sections.text: The evergreen leaves cluster at the ends of branches. Small flowers appear in clusters; the fleshy fruits turn orange-red when ripe.

sections.title: Resin and uses
sections.text: Its red resin, known as dragon’s blood, is harvested and used traditionally. The sources consulted do not document the tree’s parts as food.
